en: Points of Controversy The Chapter on the Decades The Seventh Section: The Decade on the Path of Certainty (Niyāma)
Discourse on Being Included:
Are there any states that are included by any other states?
Yes, they are.
Is it not the case that there are certain phenomena which are included in the reckoning of other phenomena, which are included in the enumeration, and which are included [within the world]?

Yes. If indeed there are certain phenomena which are included in the reckoning of other phenomena, which are included in the enumeration, and which are included, then surely, O friend, you should not say: [that all phenomena are unconditioned].
“There are no phenomena that are comprised by any other phenomena.
To which aggregate-count does the eye-base belong?
It belongs to the count of the aggregate of form.
If the eye-base is included in the enumeration of the form aggregate, then indeed, sir, it must be said:
"The eye-base is comprised within the form aggregate.
The ear-base... [and so on].
To which aggregate-count does the nose-base …pe… the tongue-base …pe… the body-base belong?
“It goes into the reckoning of the aggregate of form.
If the body-base (kāyāyatana) goes into the reckoning of the aggregate of form, then indeed, O sir, it must be said:
“The body-base is included within the aggregate of form.”
The base of visible forms …pe… the base of sounds …pe… the base of odors …pe…
The taste base …pe… the tangible object base— into which aggregate’s enumeration does it fall?
It falls into the enumeration of the form aggregate.
If the sense-base of the tangible goes into the counting of the aggregate of form, then indeed, sir, you must say:
"The sense-base of the tangible is included within the aggregate of form.
But into the counting of which aggregate does pleasant feeling go?
“It goes into the reckoning of the aggregate of feeling.
If pleasant feeling goes into the reckoning of the aggregate of feeling, then indeed, sir, it must be said:
“Pleasant feeling is included within the aggregate of feeling.”
Painful feeling … [and so on] … neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling: to which aggregate does it belong?
It belongs to the aggregate of feeling.
If neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling belongs to the aggregate of feeling, then indeed, sir, you must say this:
“Neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling is included within the aggregate of feeling.
To which aggregate-count does perception born of eye-contact belong?
It belongs to the count of the aggregate of perception.
If perception born of eye-contact is included in the reckoning of the aggregate of perception, then indeed it must be said:
"Perception born of eye-contact is comprised within the aggregate of perception.
[The same applies to] perception born of ear-contact... and so forth.
Into which aggregate does perception born of mind-contact fall?
It falls into the enumeration of the perception aggregate.
If perception born of mind-contact falls into the enumeration of the perception aggregate, then indeed, it must be said:
“Perception born of mind-contact is included within the aggregate of perception.
But to which aggregate-count does volition born of eye-contact … [and so on] … volition born of mind-contact belong?
"It goes into the reckoning of the aggregate of volitional formations (saṅkhārakkhandha).
If mental contact-born volition (manosamphassajā cetanā) goes into the reckoning of the aggregate of volitional formations, then indeed, it must be said:
"Mental contact-born volition is included within the aggregate of volitional formations."
Does eye-consciousness … pe … mind-consciousness go into the reckoning of which aggregate?
It goes into the reckoning of the consciousness aggregate.
If mental consciousness (manoviññāṇa) is included in the reckoning of the aggregate of consciousness (viññāṇakkhandha), then indeed, sir, it must be said:
"Mental consciousness is comprised within the aggregate of consciousness.
Just as two oxen are bound together by a rope or a cord, or as a bowl of alms-food is held by a sling, or as a dog is held by a leash.
In the same way, are those phenomena (dhammas) comprised by those [other] phenomena?
If two oxen are bound together by a halter or a rope, and a bundle of alms-food is held by a carrying-sling, and that sling is held by a leash, then indeed, my friend, you must admit:
"There are certain phenomena that are comprised by certain other phenomena."
The Discussion on Being Included is finished.
